title: KV swap heuristics and host-capacity scaling (wip)
content:
Overview:

This note collects design ideas and heuristics for an adaptive KV-cache offload and host-memory paging subsystem intended to be used by the serving runtime across heterogeneous host configurations (PCIe-attached GPUs, integrated UMA devices, multi-socket NUMA nodes). Goal: preserve tail latency SLOs for typical LLM workloads while increasing effective model context capacity by opportunistically offloading cold KV segments to host RAM and PCIe-resident staging buffers.

Motivation and constraints:
- On high-utilization clusters we frequently hit GPU memory limits for long contexts or many concurrent sessions. Naively swapping KV to host memory prevents OOM but can catastrophically increase tail latency.
- Different hardware topologies have different cost/latency for host-residency: UMA (integrated GPUs) yield low host<->device latency for pinned pages; PCIe NVLink/PCIe Gen4+ paths add tens to hundreds of microseconds per page transfer depending on size and concurrency.
- Workloads exhibit skew in KV access: most prefixes reuse a small hot set while long-tail keys are rarely referenced.
- Serving runtime must balance: immediate latency impact, aggregate bandwidth consumption, and long-term cost (CPU memory pressure, page churn).

Design principles:
1) Safety-first fallbacks: never block a critical foreground token generation to wait for a large transfer. If a needed KV segment is remote, schedule prioritized incremental transfer and fallback to a lower-cost model variant or shorter context fallback if transfer latency would exceed a threshold.
2) Predictive cold-offload: use recent access patterns to detect cold slices (low reuse over window) and proactively migrate them to host or NVMe cache during idle periods.
3) Adaptive thresholds: thresholds for offload and prefetch should be adaptive per-host based on observed PCIe round-trip and bandwidth, host memory utilization, and serving latency tail.
4) Incremental transfer units: transfer in units aligned to KV block boundaries (e.g., 4–32 KB pages aggregated into transfer batches) to avoid head-of-line blocking.
5) NUMA/UMA-aware placement: prefer host pages placed on the CPU NUMA node closest to the GPU or use hugepages when supported to reduce TLB pressure.

Components and responsibilities:
- Resident policy engine (RPE): maintains per-model/per-batch hot scores for KV slices, computes candidates for offload/prefetch, and emits actions with urgency levels (background, interactive, preemptive).
- Host pager agent (HPA): OS-level helper running in user-space to pin and stage pages, track host RAM pressure, and coordinate PCIe DMA transfers with the GPU driver.
- Transfer scheduler (TS): global on-host scheduler that sequences DMA transfers, enforces aggregate PCIe bandwidth caps, and prioritizes interactive transfers.
- Fallback selector: runtime logic that decides whether to delay token emission for transfer, to use a smaller context or a cached model variant, or to synthesize a partial response.

Heuristics and thresholds (proposed):
- Hot score window: 60s sliding window with decay alpha=0.2. Any slice with hot_score < 0.03 is "cold" candidate. Tunable per-model.
- Offload condition: offload cold slice if (GPU_free_memory < 5% of model working set) AND (host_free_memory > 2 * slice_size) AND (expected_offload_bandwidth_cost < projected_latency_benefit).
- Immediate prefetch threshold: when a request references a slice that is resident on host, compute estimated PCIe transfer latency L_est for slice batch size. If L_est < interactive_latency_budget (default 8ms) then schedule interactive DMA and wait; else trigger fallback.
- Background prefetch: use low-priority DMA windows during GPU idle cycles or when global PCIe utilization < 35% to warm host-resident slices predicted to be referenced within next N requests (N=3 by default).
- Eviction thresholds: Evict to host when local cache occupancy > 80% OR when maintenance window detected. Evict older cold slices first and avoid evicting slices with high reuse within the last 30s.

PCIe and UMA calibration:
At host startup or driver attach, run a quick micro-benchmark: several batched DMA transfers of canonical slice sizes (8KB, 32KB, 128KB, 512KB) to estimate RTT and sustained bandwidth. Expose three numbers to RPE: RTT_low (median single-batch latency), BW_sustained (MB/s under moderate concurrency), and BW_tail (bandwidth under heavy concurrency). Use these to derive L_est for arbitrary batch sizes and concurrent inflight transfers.

Transfer scheduling and isolation:
- TS enforces per-tenant and per-model bandwidth caps so a single noisy model can't saturate PCIe and starve interactive transfers. Caps derived from historical percentiles: interactive_budget = 0.2 * BW_sustained by default.
- Use credit-based pacing: each transfer consumes credits proportional to its byte-size / BW_sustained; when credits exhausted, new background transfers wait. Interactive transfers can borrow credits from a short-term emergency pool.

NUMA / UMA placement heuristics:
- For UMA devices: keep host-resident KV pages on the same NUMA node as the GPU to reduce latency; use mlock and NUMA binding where available.
- For multi-socket hosts: if host memory pressure is high on the GPU-local NUMA node, prefer remote-node eviction only after local reclaim attempts; track cross-node transfer penalty and prefer compressing remote pages before transfer.

Prefetch prediction model (lightweight):
- Use an LRU+frequency hybrid: track second-chance counters for slices; raise prefetch score if slice referenced by >=2 distinct requests within window.
- Complement with simple n-gram of recent token prefixes at request time to signal imminent reuse (cheap hashed prefix index).

Fallback strategies (ordered by desirability):
1) Non-blocking immediate generation using a cached prefix-only model variant (no KV slice load).
2) Partial wait with incremental token streaming: emit tokens that don't require the missing slice while transfer proceeds.
3) Synchronous wait up to an interactive cap (default 8ms) for the transfer.
4) Use smaller context (drop oldest slices) and annotate response with partial-context warning.

Testing plan and metrics:
- Unit microbenchmarks for transfer latency and concurrency; automated nightly runs across representative host types (UMA, PCIe x16 Gen4, PCIe x16 Gen5).
- End-to-end load tests: synthetic long-context generation with heavy cold-slice probability to measure P50/P95/P99 latencies and throughput before/after heuristics.
- Safety regression tests: blocked transfer path simulation to ensure fallbacks execute and no request stalls indefinitely.
- Key metrics to track: PCIe BW util, average transfer latency, cache hit rate (per model), evicted_bytes/sec, background_preload_bandwidth, user_visible_fallbacks/sec, tail latency with/without offload.

Operational rollout and knobs:
- Start in monitoring-only mode: enable RPE scoring and log candidate actions but do not actually offload. Use 2 weeks of telemetry to tune thresholds.
- Gradual enablement: roll to <10% traffic on a small dedicated fleet with metrics alarms for tail-latency increase >5%.
- Escalation: automatic disable if host CPU load >80% or host_free_memory < 10% for >30s.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Noisy neighbor DMA storms: mitigated by TS quotas and emergency preemption for interactive transfers.
- Host memory thrashing: when eviction leads to paging on the host, reduce offload aggressiveness and increase cold threshold.
- Driver crash mid-transfer: ensure HPA reconciles incomplete transfers and marks slices as invalid so runtime falls back safely.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we allow multi-model pooled host caches with eviction priority weighted by dollar cost (tenant billing)? Pros: higher global hit-rate. Cons: cross-tenant isolation complexity.
- Explore hardware compression on host pages (LZ4) vs GPU-side compression tradeoffs (CPU cycles vs PCIe bandwidth).
- Formalize SLO budgeting: how much PCIe budget can be purchased for interactive operations vs background without violating tail SLOs across workload mixes?
- Evaluate economic tradeoffs of reserving NIC-affinity and hugepages across clusters for lower TLB miss rates.

Appendix: example pseudo flow (simplified)
- Request arrives referencing slices A,B,C. Check local cache: A resident, B host-resident, C resident.
- RPE computes L_est for B = 12ms > interactive_budget. Fallback selector chooses partial-stream fallback.
- TS concurrently schedules a low-priority background DMA for B (credits used).
- If within 8ms B still not available and generation needs B for next token, use cached-model variant path.

Notes on tuning values: All thresholds above are draft defaults from small-scale experiments. Real deployment should auto-calibrate using the calibration micro-benchmark and rolling telemetry.
